title: Mirabel and the Drop
premise: Jonah Fairweather has spent six years as the invisible fixer for the Meridian Office, an embassy that exists on no map, keeping a go-bag packed and her real name buried. When a real-estate listing surfaces with interior photos of her safe house, she realizes someone inside sold her out, and the buyer is the assassin who killed her predecessor. Racing a border checkpoint rotation that will seal her in, Jonah must smuggle the truth past three governments that all prefer her silence, leaning on a found family of fellow unpersons: a defected analyst, a burned journalist, and the checkpoint guard who once owed her. She trades her invisibility for the truth, exposing the Office at the checkpoint itself, surviving the assassin, and finally claiming a name, a home, and a family that knows exactly who she is.
about_author: S. M. Montrose is the pen name of a former diplomatic security consultant who spent a decade in cities that appear on no official itineraries. They now write thrillers from a coastal town where, they insist, the go-bag is finally unpacked.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Scrolling a property site at 3 a.m., she finds her safe house listed with photos of her own toothbrush, her maps, her life. The emotional beat is cold vertigo: six years of invisibility ending in a click. She burns the go-bag's paper trail and calls a dead man's number.

chapters.title: Meridian Office Rules
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, flashback woven in. She reports the breach to Deputy Chief Aldous Renk, who offers reassurance that feels like a leash. We learn the Office's rules: no names, no debts, no exits. Beat: her loyalty tested against the first flicker of doubt.

chapters.title: The Buyer's Agent
chapters.summary: Jonah surveils the listing agent, a cheerful woman named Petra, and finds a payment trail leading to Vasko Ilic, the assassin who killed her predecessor, Mara. Beat: grief sharpened into purpose. First hint that Mara left something hidden in the house.

chapters.title: Go-Bag
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She retrieves her go-bag from a train locker and finds it has been opened and resealed, expertly. Inside, a note in Mara's handwriting: 'Ask the checkpoint.' Beat: dread and a strange inheritance; Mara knew she would die.

chapters.title: The Analyst Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: POV shift to Odile Ferrand, a defected analyst hiding in a laundromat basement. Odile recognizes the safe house from a leaked dossier and realizes Jonah is the fixer in file forty-one. Beat: two ghosts recognizing each other; Odile decides to make contact.

chapters.title: Laundromat Parley
chapters.summary: Jonah and Odile meet under fluorescent light, each holding a knife under the table. Odile reveals the dossier: the Office doesn't just fix problems, it manufactures the crises it's paid to resolve. Beat: loyalty cracking; Jonah defends the Office out of habit and hates herself for it.

chapters.title: Three Governments
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She maps who wants the house: a domestic ministry, a foreign intelligence service, and a private security consortium, each believing the other bought it. The listing was a message meant to start a war between them. Beat: scale widens; she is a pawn being moved.

chapters.title: Renk's Kindness
chapters.summary: Jonah confronts Renk with the dossier. He is warm, paternal, devastating: he admits the Office manufactures crises, and offers her Mara's old desk if she stays silent. Beat: the seduction of belonging; the family that raised her is asking her to lie.

chapters.title: The Journalist in Exile
chapters.summary: POV shift to Tomas Reyes, a burned journalist living off credit cards that shouldn't work. Jonah recruits him to authenticate the dossier. Beat: cautious hope; Tomas's cynicism meets Jonah's discipline and they recognize fellow unpersons.

chapters.title: House of Photographs
chapters.summary: Jonah breaks into her own safe house, now staged for sale. She finds Mara's cache behind a baseboard: a ledger of every manufactured crisis, keyed to checkpoint logs. Ilic nearly catches her; she escapes through a neighbor's garden. Beat: terror braided with resolve.

chapters.title: The Checkpoint Guard
chapters.summary: POV shift to Sergeant Anka Voss at the border checkpoint, who owes Jonah a debt from a night Jonah won't discuss. Anka notices the rotation schedule changed, the checkpoint will seal for 72 hours tomorrow night. Beat: the clock starts; loyalty called in.

chapters.title: Petra's Confession
chapters.summary: Jonah corners Petra, the agent, who confesses she was hired to photograph the house by a man with a Meridian lanyard, someone inside. Beat: betrayal lands close to home; Jonah realizes the listing was Renk's message to flush her out.

chapters.title: What Odile Saw
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She decodes the ledger: the next manufactured crisis is scheduled at the checkpoint, timed to the 72-hour closure, a false flag that will kill dozens and bury the Office's enemies. Beat: moral stakes crystallize; silence now has a body count.

chapters.title: Renk Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Her accounts freeze, her contacts go dark, and Ilic is waiting outside Tomas's flat. Renk calls: come home, bring the ledger, we'll protect you. Beat: the false embrace; she understands the family was always a trap with warm lighting.

chapters.title: The Burned and the Buried
chapters.summary: The found family gathers in the laundromat: Odile, Tomas, and Jonah plan to move the ledger through the sealed checkpoint before the false flag. Beat: belonging chosen, not assigned; each offers what they have and keeps nothing back.

chapters.title: Ilic at the Door
chapters.summary: Ilic finds them. A brutal close-quarters fight in the laundromat; Odile is wounded covering Tomas's escape with a copy of the ledger. Jonah lets Ilic live long enough to learn who hired him: not Renk. The consortium. Beat: the enemy of her enemy is not her friend.

chapters.title: The Deal Nobody Wanted
chapters.summary: Jonah offers the ledger to the foreign intelligence service in exchange for the checkpoint staying open one hour. They accept and plan to take the ledger and let the false flag proceed. Beat: bitter pragmatism; she is playing the same game she hates.

chapters.title: Seventy-Two Hours
chapters.summary: Anka's POV. The checkpoint seals. Anka finds the schedule anomaly, a cargo lane reserved for a truck that shouldn't exist, and must decide whether to trust a woman she's met twice. Beat: quiet courage; the debt repaid in advance.

chapters.title: The Truck
chapters.summary: Climax begins. The false-flag truck rolls toward the checkpoint crowd. Jonah, wounded, intercepts it with Anka's help while Odile, from a hospital bed, feeds the ledger to every press outlet Tomas can reach. Beat: everything converges at the barrier.

chapters.title: Truth at the Barrier
chapters.summary: Climax. Jonah forces the truck open before the crowd and the cameras, exposing the staged device as Renk arrives to contain it. Renk offers her one last belonging: come home, we were your family. She answers by handing the ledger to a journalist. Ilic, ordered to clean up, instead walks away. Beat: loyalty finally aligned with truth.

chapters.title: After the Sale
chapters.summary: Falling action. The consortium burns, Renk vanishes, three governments issue three different denials. Jonah, Odile, and Tomas share a meal in a real house with curtains and no cameras. Beat: exhaustion, grief for Mara, and the strange lightness of being seen.

chapters.title: A Name, Spoken Aloud
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, final. At a small registry office she reclaims her birth name, with Odile and Tomas as witnesses. The go-bag stays packed, out of habit, but under the bed. Beat: resolution and earned peace; belonging is no longer something she hides from.
